knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{3}{2}$.

m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(0\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(0\right)+\left(-1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} - 1
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=-1$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- x^{2} - x$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=- 2 x - 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=- 2 \left(-1\right) - 1=1
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(1\right)}=-1.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(0\right)&=-1\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=- x+\left(-1\right)+\left(0\right)\\
y&=- x - 1
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=-1$ and $b=-1$.
